opex.name: Operating expenses
opex.note: Research, engineering and running the business side of the fabs — shown as one line, including other operating income and expenses, net.

follow100Note: Of every $100 of revenue, $38.05 stayed as profit; high-performance computing alone brought in $46 of it, and advanced 7nm-and-below nodes were 65% of wafer revenue.
footerNote: TSMC reports in New Taiwan dollars (revenue NT$592.6B; net income attributable to shareholders NT$225.5B). Dollar figures are converted at NT$31.41 per US$1 — implied by TSMC's own stated US-dollar revenue of $18.87B (NT$ revenue divided by that figure). Operating expenses are shown as one line combining operating expenses with other operating income and expenses, net, as in TSMC's consolidated financial statements. Segment dollars are TSMC's official platform revenues for the quarter converted at the same rate (platform shares: high-performance computing 46%, smartphone 38%, Internet of Things 6%, automotive 6%, digital consumer electronics 2%, others 2%). The tax line is set so the flow lands on net income attributable to TSMC shareholders.
otherDetail: Non-operating income of NT$17.5B (about $0.6B) — mostly NT$19.4B of interest earned on TSMC's large cash pile, plus a NT$3.2B foreign-exchange gain and NT$0.9B share of profits from associates, partly offset by NT$3.3B of other losses and NT$2.7B of finance costs.

sources.label: Official earnings release with Q2 guidance (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: High-performance computing — mostly AI accelerators — was 46% of revenue and grew 3% from the fourth quarter, while smartphone chips fell 16% in their seasonal lull and still made up another 38%.
takeaways.title: AI demand cushioned the phone dip

takeaways.text: Gross margin was 53.1% and operating margin 42.0% — both down from a year earlier (56.3% and 45.5%) as newer fabs ramped — yet net income still rose 9% on 16.5% revenue growth.
takeaways.title: Margins eased from a year ago

takeaways.text: Management guided second-quarter revenue to $19.6–20.4B with a gross margin of 51–53%, expecting strong demand for its industry-leading 3nm and 5nm technologies to outweigh continued smartphone seasonality.
takeaways.title: A bigger Q2 guided

verdict: TSMC's revenue rose 16.5% to NT$592.6B ($18.9B) as continued demand for AI and high-performance computing chips softened a seasonal smartphone dip — and with a 53.1% gross margin, it kept NT$225.5B ($7.2B) as profit, up 9%.
